scenario: Industry standard for DAF administrators and philanthropic advisers
leading_indicators: Sponsors or broker-dealers require or reimburse it; FINRA listing; CFP Board CE approval; College publishes holder counts; DAFCP appears in postings
supporting_evidence: Only DAF-specific designation; established issuer; recurring PRP; sponsor-funded Forum aligned to curriculum
counterarguments: No entry requirement; no third-party accreditation; CAP after 20+ years is only 'preferred'; thin reception
likely_beneficiaries: College; sponsors that shape the content; early holders
risks: Locks in sponsor-friendly framing as the professional baseline

leading_indicators: Holders mostly use it on bios and LinkedIn; no change in sponsor or vendor selection; continued release-driven coverage
supporting_evidence: Practice-building framing in launch ('market-proof their practices'); low cost and no prerequisite; ThinkAdvisor 'alphabet soup' context
counterarguments: Early visible holders are sponsor staff, not advisers
risks: Credential inflation; little measurable competence gain

scenario: Specialised credential for complex-gift, sponsor-staff and gift-planning roles
leading_indicators: Sponsor and community-foundation staff cohorts; nonprofit discount uptake; complex-asset sessions at the Forum
supporting_evidence: Curriculum strongest on complex assets; faculty cluster from noncash administration; nonprofit pricing; early holders at sponsors
counterarguments: Small addressable market; CAP already serves gift planners
risks: Narrow market may not sustain the product

scenario: Limited adoption; fails to differentiate from CAP, CFP and sponsor CE
leading_indicators: No holder counts by 2027-28; Forum attendance low; DAFCP folded into CAP or CE
supporting_evidence: Indifference signals; free sponsor CE and DAFopedia substitutes; College operating deficits
counterarguments: First-mover status; sponsor-funded Forum gives a distribution channel
likely_beneficiaries: Sponsors (their own CE remains the default)
